items.title: The dimension inequality for a dominant locally finite type morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the dimension inequality for a dominant morphism of integral schemes which is locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian base: the dimension of the source is at most the dimension of the target plus the transcendence degree of the function field extension, with equality when the morphism is closed. The proof takes a chain of specialisations in the source, bounds its length by the dimension of the local ring at its end point, then applies the dimension formula for the local rings at a point and its image, and drops the nonnegative correction term to get the inequality; the equality case is then derived in the remainder of the argument.
